title: Telemachus Lands in Secret
part: The four books with no filmed scene (3, 7, 15, 20): Book 15's key scene, filmed for the first time
hypothesis: The landing reads as an omen and a parting if the hawk with the dove in its talons is seen crossing the sky on his right and the feathers fall between him and the ship, the seer reads it to him, and he is seen giving his orders, handing the seer to Piraeus and walking off alone.
variable: First take: the hawk with the dove (tools/forage/keyprops.js hawkDove) and its feathers flown by FLY; Piraeus and two of the crew added to the cast (film-readymades/staging.py); the action staged on the open grass between the beached ship and the ruin, the cameras from the open side; the hawk-and-dove narration restored to the cut. Before the render: the feathers at half size (they had fallen past the lens as plates as big as a head), no over-the-heads cameras (solve.js noHigh). After the first render the last shot (a far wide, still 0.87) was re-shot alone as a mid on Telemachus (the other 494 drawings seeded from the first render).
held: the set: the forage's landing (a beached hull, a tree and a ruin)
the lens set and the solver; the homeostat not run (compiler defaults)

voice.cut: the Regulars' Cut (gi 2, 4, 5) with the hawk and the dove (gi 1) restored

captions: Narrator: As the ship approaches Ithaca, a hawk tears a dove beside Telemachus.
Narrator: Theoclymenus reads the omen as proof that Odysseus's line will remain supreme.
Telemachus: Crew, take her round to the town harbor without me ...
Narrator: Telemachus entrusts Theoclymenus to Piraeus and walks inland alone.
sheets: scratchpad w/sheets/b15s05-sheet.jpg, b15s05-every.jpg (every 2 s), b15s05-omen.jpg (2.5-8.5 s at 3 fps), b15s05-end.jpg (38-44 s at 3 fps)

result: Kept. The hawk with the dove in its talons crosses the sky over the seer and the feathers come down between them; the seer reads it in close; Telemachus gives the crew their orders (they answer, moving), gives the seer into Piraeus's keeping and walks off along the shore (38.7-41.2 s, a wide that moves). Loose: the hawk and dove are small against the ruin's dark arch; the feathers read as small white plates; the seer's reading has no line of his own (the narrator tells it); the last shot is Telemachus with his hand up to the crew, standing, not walking inland; several frames have a crewman's head large in the foreground (20-27 s).
